audited_inflection_rules.text: Use four principal parts. Present 1sg/pl use the present stem; present 2/3sg have the audited mutation/consonant changes. Past1/3sg normally share the singular stem; past2sg uses the plural stem plus -e, and all plural persons use -on. findan requires the separately printed exception.
Infinitive and past participle are citation/reference support only. No new perfect, passive, infinitive clause, participial agreement or prefix rule follows from a principal-parts table.
Class I normally ī : ā : i : i. Snīðan changes ð to d in plural-based past forms and participle. Contracted wrēon has a special present and h/g stems.
Class II normally ēo or ū : ēa : u : o. Present2/3sg ēo→īe and ū→ȳ; Cook also allows ī for īe. cēosan s/r, sēoðan ð/d, and tēon h/g are lexical changes.

III has several present/past-singular families, not one interchangeable vowel formula: bindan i/a/u/u, helpan e/ea/u/o, gieldan ie/ea/u/o, weorpan eo/ea/u/o, berstan e/æ/u/o. All those selected vowels are short. weorðan adds ð/d; winnan reduces nn; findan, bregdan and fēolan need explicit exception notes.

Dental d/t+ð gives tt (or t); d+st gives tst. s+st/ð gives st; ð before st may disappear and ð+ð may reduce. Geminates reduce before consonantal endings. g/h alternatives require the stated long-vowel/liquid environment; do not substitute h indiscriminately.

Cook permits full -est/-eð forms as well as syncopated cells. Their vowel can preserve an older mutated stem or be restored analogically; the audit selects complete contracted rows and records specifically checked variants rather than generating every possible full-ending spelling. A correct documented variant is not wrong merely for differing from the recall target.

Recognize present plural -e before an immediately following subject pronoun (Cook binde wē). This is conditioned by word order and is not a global alternative to -að after a preceding subject; production tasks may retain subject-before-verb.

Tōberstan and forweorðan are independently sourced lexemes, then expanded by identified base morphology. Their meanings and intransitive source frames are separate. No arbitrary prefix attachment or sense composition is licensed.
Extend prior preverbal ne to the introduced noncontracting strong indicatives. Keep negative copula, nillan and other contracted systems outside this extension.
Ordinary weorðan become can take a nominative predicate adjective agreeing with the subject. The finite indicative system does not promote old supplied passive constructions.

The finite paradigm does not establish object case. In particular helpan permits genitive or dative (selected dative here); bēodan command, gieldan repayment, bregdan instrumental use and other complements require separate teaching. Morphology-only verbs may be practised with person/tense labels without composing an unsupported clause.

finite.obligation: Show complete present and past indicative endings with every person/number, explicitly explaining dual pronouns take plural verbs (already taught).

All24 productive systems must be recoverable exactly: eight surface columns per lemma are sufficient; merge past1/3 only when actually equal and retain an explicit findan exception. No isolated principal-parts list substitutes for present2/3sg.
Show complete bregdan and fēolan systems separately with evidence/variant limits and recognition-only labels; do not grade independent recall.
Give four principal parts, naming finite vs citation-only nonfinite entries. Keep source variants and prefixed lexical systems explicit.

constructions.description: Two sentences contain six coordinated finite indicative predicates. The final ūpēode retains Apollonius as understood subject; an adverb may precede its verb. No subordinate, imperative, subjunctive, passive, perfect or infinitive construction occurs in the selected span.
constructions.scope_limit: Prior coordination and recognition of source order do not impose a universal inversion rule.

constructions.description: tōberstan = break up/go to pieces and forweorðan = perish are intransitive: scip is subject of tōbærst; gefēran is subject of forwurdon. Teach their full checked ClassIII indicative systems as distinct lexemes.
constructions.scope_limit: Full finite paradigms are owned by the independent Unit4 grammar audit; no general productive prefix rule or auxiliary use is licensed.

constructions.description: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan means in addition to that/besides: further winds join the already described storm. The preceding storm is summarized in separate English editorial context.
constructions.scope_limit: Fixed connective supplied; no productive compound-adverb rule.

constructions.description: him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them. ongēan follows its dative pronoun. The natural local reading takes him as the preceding northeast winds, but its spelling also permits masculine/neuter singular and the antecedent is an editorial inference, not morphologically unique.
constructions.scope_limit: Do not demand unique number/antecedent identification from him alone; do not teach general postposition syntax. A justified alternative antecedent is not rejected solely for differing from the guiding inference.

constructions.description: ðæt scip eall = the whole ship/all the ship. eall is strong neuter nominative singular, postposed to the subject noun phrase; its morphology/sense were recognition-only in Unit3.
constructions.scope_limit: Keep eall morphology and sense at their prior recognition milestone; the postposed whole/all construction is supplied, not independent production.

constructions.description: on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible tempest/storm. The noun phrase is feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after the demonstrative. This abstract surrounding circumstance is supplied locally.
constructions.scope_limit: Prior spatial on+dative does not automatically establish every figurative/circumstantial sense.

constructions.description: Apollonius gefēran = Apollonius’s companions. Cook note1 explicitly identifies the foreign proper name here as genitive despite its -us appearance. gefēran is nominative plural, not a subject named Apollonius.
constructions.scope_limit: The relation and before-head placement are prior; the actual foreign-name case form is supplied. No complete Latin-name declension is introduced.

constructions.description: gefēran ealle = all the companions. ealle is strong masculine nominative plural agreeing with gefēran; the all-quantifier construction remains supplied.
constructions.scope_limit: Prior recognition of ealle is not new productive quantifier mastery.

constructions.description: forwurdon tō dēaðe = perished to death, naturally all died/perished. dēaðe is masculine dative singular; tō states the endpoint/result, not an infinitive marker or the previously supplied function-for sense.
constructions.scope_limit: Supply this tō phrase whole; no general goal/result construction is assumed.

constructions.description: Apollonius āna = Apollonius alone. āna is weak masculine nominative singular of ān in its alone sense, agreeing with the sole survivor; it is not cardinal one or the homographic feminine plural reference form.
constructions.scope_limit: New sense and weak form are supplied only; Unit3 productive cardinal ān does not cover them.

constructions.description: becōm mid sunde = came/arrived by swimming. sund is a neuter noun; sunde is dative singular after mid. This means phrase is not an infinitive or newly productive instrumental construction.
constructions.scope_limit: Supply actual mid sunde; do not infer a productive swimming verb or general mid syntax.

constructions.description: tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. The foreign place name occupies the destination position; the native appositional phrase is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan. Preserve the foreign -im spelling rather than treating it as a native OE accusative-governance rule.
constructions.scope_limit: Exact destination/apposition is supplied. No general foreign-name declension or productive tō-goal syntax.

constructions.description: and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande = and there he came/went up onto the shore. Apollonius remains the understood subject. ūpēode is the actual anomalous preterite of ūpgān; strande is masculine dative singular in the printed local on phrase.
constructions.scope_limit: Supply ūpēode and ðǣr; preserve dative strande and do not replace it with accusative from a modern English motion gloss.

local_support.text: Ðǣr-tō-ēacan = in addition to that/besides; the storm has already begun.
cōmon = came, third-person plural past of cuman (ClassIV); ēastnorðerne = northeasterly, masculine nominative plural.

angrīslica = fierce/raging; sūðwesterna = southwestern, both weak masculine nominative singular with wind. him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them: guiding reference, the northeast winds. The pronoun spelling alone does not exclude a singular referent; no uniquely graded antecedent is required.
eall = whole/all, neuter nominative singular agreeing with scip. This local quantifier use is supplied; its earlier morphology was recognition only.
on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible storm: feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after ðisse.
Apollonius before gefēran is genitive, Apollonius’s, as Cook note1 specifies. ealle = all, masculine nominative plural agreeing with the companions; quantifier use remains supplied.
tō dēaðe = to death, with dative singular dēaðe; the whole expression means that the companions died/perished.

The next Apollonius is nominative. āna = alone, weak masculine nominative singular, a distinct sense/form from cardinal one. becōm = came/arrived (third-person singular past, ClassIV). mid sunde = by swimming: dative noun sunde, not an infinitive.
tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. Preserve the foreign name; the native apposition is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan.

ðǣr = there; ūpēode = he came/went up (anomalous past of ūpgān), with Apollonius understood. on ðǣm strande = on the shore, masculine dative singular as printed; do not replace the ending from the English gloss came ashore.

grammar_inventory.description: Identify the four principal-part positions and distinguish finite preterite entries from supplied infinitive/participle citations.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No unaided nonfinite recall, infinitive complement, participial agreement, perfect or passive syntax.

grammar_inventory.description: Distinguish strong preterite ablaut from the previously taught weak dental preterite.
Complete selected present and preterite indicative: all three persons, singular and plural; these tables introduce no other mood or nonfinite construction.
Present 1sg -e, 2sg -st and 3sg -ð with each audited stem/consonant adjustment; ordinary plural -að and the selected contracted plurals.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Postposed-pronoun plural -e is outside assigned learner scope, not a free alternative.

grammar_inventory.description: Past 1/3sg normally use the singular stem; 2sg uses the plural stem with -e and all plural persons use -on; findan has its separately taught selected exception.
Selected Class I ī : ā : i : i principal-part pattern, present stem and exact finite paradigms.
Selected Class II ēo/ū : ēa : u : o pattern, including its exact lexical singular present mutation.
Selected nasal Class III i : a : u : u finite systems (bindan, winnan, findan, drincan, singan), retaining lexical exceptions.
Helpan e/ea/u and gieldan ie/ea/u finite families with their distinct present singulars; selected vowels are short.
Weorpan and weorðan eo/ea/u finite family and separately audited forweorðan; present singular mutation remains lexical.
Berstan and separately audited tōberstan use e/æ/u with the selected metathesized order and present bierst.
The selected II and III second/third singular present vowels differ from present1/pl; exact lexical diagnostics, not an unrestricted replacement rule.
Audited dental/sibilant contractions, ð-stem effects, geminate reduction and bounded g/h variants in selected present2/3sg.
Lexical consonant alternation: snīðan/sēoðan/weorðan ð/d; cēosan s/r; contracted stems h/g, at their explicitly mapped positions.
Complete wrēon indicative with wrēo/wrīhst/wrīhð/wrēoð and wrāh/wrige/wrigon; no merger with the Class II homographic series.
Complete Class II tēon draw/pull indicative, with its selected contracted present and tēah/tuge/tugon past.
Select fand as past1sg, funde as past2sg and usual past3sg, fundon for all plural persons; admit first-person funde and third-person fand as documented alternatives.
Recognize complete bregdan and composite fēolan indicative references using displayed tables and their declared source/variant limits.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No independent production or unassigned clause government; Cook folen remains the citation target.

grammar_inventory.description: Tōberstan and forweorðan are separately learned whole lexemes with full berstan/weorðan finite morphology.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No productive prefix-attachment or automatic compositional-meaning rule.

grammar_inventory.description: Complete scip, wind, strand and gefēra NGDA singular/plural, using the prior complete noun patterns and independently checked lexical stems.
Selected ordinary transitive uses: drīfan drives cattle, bindan binds an animal, cēosan chooses a thing, findan finds a thing and drincan drinks water; the direct object is accusative.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact lexical government is independently evidenced. Cattle, an animal, ships and dwellings in these new compositions are declared ordinary lexical applications, not falsely attributed source quotations. No universal strong-verb accusative rule.

grammar_inventory.description: Rīdan ride and singan sing may stand without a nominal object; prior manner adverbs qualify the action.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No directional complement or instrumental transport is implied by riding.

grammar_inventory.description: Helpan takes the dative being or recipient helped in the selected ordinary use. The attested person examples support the declared new application to birds.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Dative being/recipient is the selected target. Attested human examples support the explicitly declared ordinary lexical application to birds. The documented genitive alternative is valid but is not the construction requested here.

grammar_inventory.description: Ordinary weorðan become takes a nominative predicate adjective agreeing with its subject.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: New sense weorthan-become only; supplied passive weorthan-1 is not promoted.

grammar_inventory.description: Prior preverbal ne extends explicitly to the selected noncontracting strong indicatives.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: No negative copula, nillan, other contracted systems or negative concord is introduced.

grammar_inventory.description: Use the assigned strong preterites for successive past events in independent coordinated clauses, retaining prior subject agreement and direct quotation.
The ship breaks up with tōberstan and the companions perish with forweorðan; each is an intransitive subject–verb clause.
Ðǣr-tō-ēacan means in addition to that/besides: further winds join the already described storm. The preceding storm is summarized in separate English editorial context.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Fixed connective supplied; no productive compound-adverb rule.

grammar_inventory.description: him ongēan stōd = stood against/opposed them. ongēan follows its dative pronoun. The natural local reading takes him as the preceding northeast winds, but its spelling also permits masculine/neuter singular and the antecedent is an editorial inference, not morphologically unique.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Do not demand unique number/antecedent identification from him alone; do not teach general postposition syntax. A justified alternative antecedent is not rejected solely for differing from the guiding inference.

grammar_inventory.description: ðæt scip eall = the whole ship/all the ship. eall is strong neuter nominative singular, postposed to the subject noun phrase; its morphology/sense were recognition-only in Unit3.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Keep eall morphology and sense at their prior recognition milestone; the postposed whole/all construction is supplied, not independent production.

grammar_inventory.description: on ðisse ęgeslican hrēohnesse = in this terrible tempest/storm. The noun phrase is feminine dative singular; ęgeslican is weak after the demonstrative. This abstract surrounding circumstance is supplied locally.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Prior spatial on+dative does not automatically establish every figurative/circumstantial sense.

grammar_inventory.description: Apollonius gefēran = Apollonius’s companions. Cook note1 explicitly identifies the foreign proper name here as genitive despite its -us appearance. gefēran is nominative plural, not a subject named Apollonius.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: The relation and before-head placement are prior; the actual foreign-name case form is supplied. No complete Latin-name declension is introduced.

grammar_inventory.description: gefēran ealle = all the companions. ealle is strong masculine nominative plural agreeing with gefēran; the all-quantifier construction remains supplied.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Prior recognition of ealle is not new productive quantifier mastery.

grammar_inventory.description: forwurdon tō dēaðe = perished to death, naturally all died/perished. dēaðe is masculine dative singular; tō states the endpoint/result, not an infinitive marker or the previously supplied function-for sense.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Supply this tō phrase whole; no general goal/result construction is assumed.

grammar_inventory.description: Apollonius āna = Apollonius alone. āna is weak masculine nominative singular of ān in its alone sense, agreeing with the sole survivor; it is not cardinal one or the homographic feminine plural reference form.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: New sense and weak form are supplied only; Unit3 productive cardinal ān does not cover them.

grammar_inventory.description: becōm mid sunde = came/arrived by swimming. sund is a neuter noun; sunde is dative singular after mid. This means phrase is not an infinitive or newly productive instrumental construction.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Supply actual mid sunde; do not infer a productive swimming verb or general mid syntax.

grammar_inventory.description: tō Pentapolim ðǣm Cyreniscan lande = to Pentapolis, the Cyrenian land. The foreign place name occupies the destination position; the native appositional phrase is neuter dative singular, with weak Cyreniscan. Preserve the foreign -im spelling rather than treating it as a native OE accusative-governance rule.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Exact destination/apposition is supplied. No general foreign-name declension or productive tō-goal syntax.

grammar_inventory.description: and ðǣr ūpēode on ðǣm strande = and there he came/went up onto the shore. Apollonius remains the understood subject. ūpēode is the actual anomalous preterite of ūpgān; strande is masculine dative singular in the printed local on phrase.
grammar_inventory.scope_note: Supply ūpēode and ðǣr; preserve dative strande and do not replace it with accusative from a modern English motion gloss.
